# Related papers (183)

English · [简体中文](../zh/related.md) · [Back to the list](../../README.md)

Papers in the collection that fall outside its focus on looped language models: loops in other domains and modalities, puzzle and grid reasoners (Sudoku, maze, ARC) such as HRM and TRM, RNN-, CNN- and GNN-era precursors, implicit models outside language, layer sharing used only to save parameters, and adjacent latent reasoning without loops. They are not ranked and not counted in the design space.

| 2026-05-08 | [Bifurcation Models: Learning Set-Valued Solution Maps with Weight-Tied Dynamics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.07277)<br><sub>Caleb Jore et al.</sub> | Bifurcation models iterate a weight-tied update so different initializations converge to different stable equilibria; the paper proves this represents broad set-valued maps with locally Lipschitz branches, and on frustrated Ising models the dynamics find multiple valid equilibria without branch labels. | [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.07277) | cites 1 |
| 2024-10-15 | [Advancing the Understanding of Fixed Point Iterations in Deep Neural Networks: A Detailed Analytical Study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.11279)<br><sub>Yekun Ke et al.</sub> | For a looped network repeatedly applying one layer g(Wx+b), gives a sufficient condition for multiple fixed points depending on the input region, extends it to robust fixed points, and shows such networks may have 2^d robust fixed points (d: feature dimension) under polynomial or exponential activations. | [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.11279) | cites 13 |
| 2024-10-12 | [Looped ReLU MLPs May Be All You Need as Practical Programmable Computers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.09375)<br><sub>Yingyu Liang et al. · AISTATS 2025</sub> | Proves by construction that a looped 23-layer ReLU-MLP can emulate the SUBLEQ instruction and so act as a programmable computer, more efficiently than a looped Transformer, indicating that simple modules are more expressive than expected. | [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.09375) | cites 34 · HF upvotes 0 |
| 2024-03-01 | [Subhomogeneous Deep Equilibrium Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.00720)<br><sub>Pietro Sittoni et al.</sub> | Proves that deep equilibrium models built from subhomogeneous operators have unique fixed points, via nonlinear Perron-Frobenius theory and weaker weight assumptions than monotone-operator DEQs; SubDEQs need fewer fixed-point iterations than MonDEQ and are tested on feedforward, convolutional and graph networks. | [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.00720) · [code](https://github.com/COMPiLELab/SubDEQ) | cites 8 · stars 2 · HF upvotes 0 |
| 2022-07-15 | [Stable Invariant Models via Koopman Spectra](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.07475)<br><sub>Takuya Konishi et al. · Neural Networks 2023</sub> | SIM describes the weight-tied, infinitely deep dynamics of DEQs via Koopman and Perron-Frobenius spectra, giving models trained like feedforward networks (single-tier SIMs use three transformations) that converge to a fixed point or a broader invariant set; SIMs match or beat DEQs on several tasks. | [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.07475) | cites 6 |
| 2021-02-15 | [On the Theory of Implicit Deep Learning: Global Convergence with Implicit Layers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.07346)<br><sub>Kenji Kawaguchi · ICLR 2021</sub> | For deep equilibrium models with nonlinearity only on weights, proves that gradient dynamics reach a global optimum at a linear rate without width assumptions, and relates them to trust region Newton on a shallow layer. | [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.07346) | cites 52 |
| 2020-06-15 | [Monotone operator equilibrium networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.08591)<br><sub>Ezra Winston et al. · NeurIPS 2020</sub> | Introduces monDEQ, an implicit-depth model built on monotone operator theory whose parameterization guarantees a unique equilibrium, solved with operator-splitting methods that converge stably; it outperforms Neural ODE-based models while being more computationally efficient. | [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.08591) · [code](https://github.com/locuslab/monotone_op_net) | cites 190 · stars 54 |

| 2021-07-12 | [PonderNet: Learning to Ponder](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.05407)<br><sub>Andrea Banino et al. · ICML 2021 AutoML Workshop</sub> | PonderNet runs a step function recurrently with a learned probabilistic halting policy; it outperforms earlier adaptive-computation methods on parity, succeeds at extrapolation, and matches state-of-the-art bAbI accuracy with less compute. | [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.05407) | cites 257 · HF upvotes 0 |

| 2025-01-30 | [DeltaLLM: Compress LLMs with Low-Rank Deltas between Shared Weights](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.18596)<br><sub>Liana Mikaelyan et al.</sub> | DeltaLLM compresses pretrained LLMs by sharing weights between layers in subsequent Transformer blocks and adding low-rank delta matrices trained on approximately 30M-40M tokens; DeltaLLAMA and DeltaPHI cut parameters by 12% while retaining 90% of base Llama and Phi performance. | [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.18596) | cites 5 · HN points 2 |
| 2022-10-12 | [MiniALBERT: Model Distillation via Parameter-Efficient Recursive Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.06425)<br><sub>Mohammadmahdi Nouriborji et al.</sub> | MiniALBERT distills fully parameterised LMs such as BERT into a compact recursive student that reuses one shared Transformer layer at every iteration, optionally with per-iteration bottleneck adapters; students with no more than 18M parameters perform competitively on general and biomedical NLP tasks. | [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.06425) · [code](https://github.com/nlpie-research/MiniALBERT) | cites 12 · stars 7 |

| 2026-11-21 | [When Wrong Answers Remain Unsettled: Failure Dynamics in Recurrent Reasoners](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28971)<br><sub>Jiucheng Zang et al.</sub> | When a trained 27M-parameter HRM on Sudoku-Extreme runs its weight-tied recurrence for one more 16-segment budget, 0.95 of solved answers persist but only 0.18 of wrong ones, so at this horizon most failures are still changing rather than trapped; the solved-above-wrong ordering also holds for a second seed, TRM, Maze, GRAM-guided TRM and N-Queens. | [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28971) | cites 0 |
| 2026-11-15 | [When Does Reusing Layers Help Multimodal Embeddings?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19827)<br><sub>Zhizhang Hu et al.</sub> | Tests eleven loop designs for multimodal embeddings, proving that under forward-only attention repeated layers cannot make earlier image states query-dependent; on MMEB-V2 an added loop loses 0.46 points, while native recurrence gains +4.23 points. | [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19827) | cites 0 |
| 2026-07-13 | [The Equilibrium Is the Initialization: Lazy Identity Collapse in Physics-Structured Deep Equilibrium Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11116)<br><sub>Joyjeet Singh</sub> | On ProofWriter entailment and graph reachability, a port-Hamiltonian DEQ with a learned initialization returns its start point as the equilibrium: bypassing the solver changes test accuracy by +0.00 percentage points in 18 of 19 training runs, which the paper traces to gradient starvation. | [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11116) · [code](https://github.com/joyjeet-singh/lazy-identity-deq) | cites 0 · stars 0 · HF upvotes 0 |
| 2021-01-12 | [Of Non-Linearity and Commutativity in BERT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.04547)<br><sub>Sumu Zhao et al. · IJCNN 2021</sub> | Analyzing BERT, the paper finds its layers largely commutative, mainly due to skip connections; ALBERT-like models that repeat one fine-tuned layer 12 times fall to random guessing but improve after 3 more fine-tuning epochs, which the authors take as support for recurrent and weight-shared Transformers. | [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.04547) | cites 23 |
